steps.question: Do the genes shifted between the treated and control liver sample fall into coherent human pathways, i.e. is there a coordinated program rather than scattered single-gene noise?
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the mouse and rat WikiPathways files in the store are the wrong organism for this liver dataset
Do not run over-representation analysis on an arbitrarily thresholded DE gene list; there is no valid threshold here, so the rank-based method is required
Do not claim pathway activation or inhibition as a demonstrated treatment effect
steps.description:
Take the full gene-level log2FC ranking from T1S2 (all filtered genes, ranked by log2FC, gene symbols as identifiers) and run a rank-based gene set enrichment (GSEA preranked, e.g. gseapy.prerank or fgsea) against human pathway gene sets. Use the human WikiPathways collection available in the reference store at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt — parse the '%'-delimited first field to recover a readable pathway name, and confirm the file is present before use. The gene symbols in the counts file are the identifier space, matching the HGNC symbols in that GMT; report the fraction of ranked genes that map into the collection and drop unmatched symbols with a count. Restrict to gene sets of 15-500 members. Report normalized enrichment scores, nominal p-values and FDR from the permutation null, and leading-edge genes for the top up- and down-shifted pathways, with a dot plot of the top 20 by |NES| and an enrichment plot for the top 3.

Interpretation constraint: the permutation statistics test whether the ranking is non-random with respect to set membership; they do NOT recover the biological replication the underlying ranking lacks. Every enrichment result must be reported as exploratory hypothesis generation. If the WikiPathways human GMT is absent at run time, report that and fall back to any other human pathway or GO gene-set collection the environment holds, naming the substitute; if none is available, report the gap rather than fabricating a collection.
acceptance_criteria: Preranked GSEA is run on the complete T1S2 log2FC ranking, not on a truncated top-gene list
The human (not mouse or rat) WikiPathways GMT is used and its path and gene-set count after 15-500 size filtering are reported
Symbol-mapping rate into the collection is reported with the number of unmatched symbols dropped
Table of pathways with NES, nominal p, FDR and leading-edge genes is written to disk
Dot plot of top 20 pathways by |NES| and enrichment plots for the top 3 are produced
Results are labelled exploratory, with an explicit note that enrichment permutation p-values do not compensate for n=1 per condition

plan.title: Treated vs control liver: 1v1 unreplicated DE screen
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 3 raw salmon count CSV (first column gene symbol, one column per sample) plus a 2 x 2 metadata table describing exactly one treated and one control human liver sample. With n=1 per condition there is no within-group variance, so no method can estimate dispersion from the data and no p-value or FDR from a two-group test is valid. Any plan that runs DESeq2/edgeR with a design of ~condition here would either fail outright or emit p-values that are pure fabrication. The plan therefore does what the data can actually support and says plainly what it cannot.

T1S1 normalizes the two libraries (CPM/median-of-ratios size factors on the raw counts), filters low-count genes, and quantifies the technical comparability of the two libraries (library sizes, detected genes, MA-plot trend, Spearman/Pearson correlation on log counts) — this is the honest QC that decides whether a fold-change ranking is even interpretable. T1S2 produces the primary deliverable: a per-gene ranked table of log2 fold change (treated vs control) with pseudocount-shrunk and expression-filtered estimates, explicitly labelled a descriptive ranking, not a statistical test. As a secondary, clearly-labelled exploratory device it also runs edgeR exactTest with a fixed, assumed BCV (the edgeR manual's convention for unreplicated designs, e.g. BCV 0.4 for human tissue and a 0.2 sensitivity check), reporting how the top-gene list moves with the assumed dispersion — this is a sensitivity analysis of an assumption, not evidence. T2S1 then takes the ranked log2FC vector into a rank-based gene set enrichment against human WikiPathways (present at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human), because a coordinated pathway-level shift is more robust to single-sample noise than any individual gene call; its statistics are permutation-based over gene ranks and are also to be reported as exploratory, since the underlying ranking has no replication behind it.

The deliverable is a prioritized candidate list plus an explicit statement of what replication would be required to test it. No step will report an FDR-controlled DE gene set as if it were established.
